skill.description: Design React Server Components, Server Actions, streaming interfaces, routing, and data fetching with the Next.js App Router.
skill.summary: Build server-first Next.js applications with practical React Server Component patterns, templates, examples, and migration guidance.
skill.author: AI Agent Hub

security_audit.summary: All 127 static alerts are false positives caused by documentation formatting, standard React patterns, placeholder fetch calls, or server-only environment access. Manual review found stored cross-site scripting, missing authorization, mass assignment, and draft disclosure in the supplied examples. These examples require security hardening before publication.

remediation.issue: The blog example renders stored post content through dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization.
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize HTML with a strict server-side allowlist before storage or rendering. Prefer a renderer that escapes raw HTML by default.

remediation.issue: Several mutating Server Actions omit authentication, authorization, and ownership checks.
remediation.suggestion: Authenticate every action, enforce resource ownership or roles, and scope database mutations to the authorized principal.

remediation.issue: Resource update actions pass caller-provided Partial<Resource> values directly to Prisma.
remediation.suggestion: Validate update payloads with a strict schema and map only approved fields into database operations.

remediation.issue: The public blog detail query does not require published status.
remediation.suggestion: Filter public queries by published status. Allow draft access only after an explicit author or administrator authorization check.

**Key Rule**: Server Components can render Client Components, but Client Components cannot directly
- ✅ Pass Server Components as `children` to Client Components
- **`templates/ServerComponent.tsx`** - Basic async Server Component with data fetching
- **`templates/ServerAction.tsx`** - Server Action with validation and revalidation
- **Fix**: Add `'use client'` directive to the component
- **Fix**: Pass Server Component as `children` prop instead of importing
- **Fix**: Use `'use client'` for components using `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, or browser APIs
- ❌ Avoid making entire pages Client Components

semantic_findings.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting in Blog Example
semantic_findings.description: The blog example stores author-supplied post content and renders it as raw HTML without sanitization. Script-bearing content could execute in readers' browsers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The input schema accepts unrestricted content, stores it, and later passes it directly to dangerouslySetInnerHTML. No sanitization step appears in the example.

semantic_findings.title: Missing Authorization in Mutating Server Actions
semantic_findings.description: Several exported Server Actions create, delete, toggle, bulk-update, upload, or revalidate without authentication or authorization. Remote callers could abuse these mutation endpoints.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: These functions are exported from a use-server module and perform privileged operations without calling the session or ownership checks shown in updateResource.

semantic_findings.title: Mass Assignment in Resource Update Actions
semantic_findings.description: Update actions accept Partial<Resource> and pass it directly to database operations without an allowlist schema. Callers could modify fields outside the intended form.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exported actions accept caller-provided partial database records and use them as update data. No Zod schema or field allowlist constrains these values.

semantic_findings.title: Unpublished Blog Posts Exposed by Slug
semantic_findings.description: The public post page loads any post matching a slug without requiring published status. Anyone who learns a draft slug could read unpublished content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The listing and static-parameter queries filter published posts, but the page query uses only the slug and renders the returned record without an access check.

content.user_title: Build React Server Components with Next.js
content.value_statement: Server and client boundaries are difficult to design correctly in modern React applications. This skill provides Next.js patterns, templates, examples, and migration guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains Server Component and Client Component boundaries.
Shows caching, revalidation, parallel fetching, and streaming patterns.
Provides templates for Server Components, Client Components, and Server Actions.
Demonstrates App Router routing, metadata, loading, and error patterns.
Guides incremental migration from the Pages Router.
Supplies an implementation checklist for architecture and performance reviews.
limitations: The guidance targets Next.js App Router projects and does not cover every React framework.
Examples require project-specific database, authentication, storage, and validation implementations.
Some supplied security examples require authorization and output-sanitization fixes before production use.
Framework APIs may change after the documented Next.js version.

use_cases.title: Design a New App Router Feature
use_cases.description: Choose server and client boundaries, data-fetching strategies, caching rules, and Suspense placement for a new feature.

use_cases.title: Review Server-First Architecture
use_cases.description: Evaluate an application for excessive client JavaScript, data waterfalls, unsafe mutations, and weak route organization.

use_cases.title: Plan a Pages Router Migration
use_cases.description: Map legacy data methods, layouts, metadata, and API mutations to App Router equivalents in controlled stages.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Component Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which parts of my feature should be Server Components or Client Components. Ask for missing interaction and data requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn the basic RSC decision process.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Server-First Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an App Router feature for [feature]. Include component boundaries, data fetching, caching, loading, error, and mutation behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a new feature before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate a Pages Router Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged migration plan for this Pages Router route. Map data methods, layouts, metadata, API routes, tests, and rollback points.
prompt_templates.scenario: Move an existing route to the App Router.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an RSC Codebase
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Next.js codebase for boundary errors, waterfalls, cache mistakes, unsafe Server Actions, data exposure, and unnecessary client bundles. Prioritize findings by severity.
prompt_templates.scenario: Perform an advanced architecture and security review.

output_examples.input: Review a dashboard that fetches all data in one client-side effect.
output: Move independent queries into Server Components near their views.
Start independent requests together to avoid a sequential waterfall.
Keep filters and interactive controls in small Client Components.
Add separate Suspense boundaries for slow dashboard sections.

output_examples.input: Plan migration of a product page from getServerSideProps.
output: Create an async App Router page that reads the product on the server.
Define cache behavior from the product freshness requirement.
Move metadata generation into the route metadata function.
Retain interactive selectors as focused Client Components.

output_examples.input: Review Server Actions for a resource editor.
output: Require authentication at the start of every mutation.
Check resource ownership inside the database mutation scope.
Validate an explicit field allowlist before updating records.
Revalidate only affected paths or tags after success.

best_practices: Use Server Components by default and keep Client Components focused on interaction.
Validate and authorize every Server Action before performing mutations.
Choose caching and Suspense boundaries from explicit freshness and loading requirements.
anti_patterns: Do not convert entire pages to Client Components for one interactive control.
Do not pass unvalidated client payloads directly into database mutations.
Do not render stored HTML without strict sanitization.

faq.question: Which framework does this skill target?
faq.answer: It primarily targets Next.js 15 App Router projects using React Server Components and Server Actions.

faq.question: Can it decide Server and Client Component boundaries?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses data access, interactivity, browser APIs, serialization, and bundle impact to guide boundary decisions.

faq.question: Does it support Pages Router migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps legacy data methods, layouts, metadata, and API routes to App Router patterns.

faq.question: Does it provide production-ready application code?
faq.answer: It provides adaptable templates and examples. Projects must supply dependencies, domain models, authentication, authorization, sanitization, testing, and deployment configuration.

faq.question: Does the skill require network access?
faq.answer: The guidance itself is local documentation. Generated applications may use network requests when their data sources require them.

faq.question: How should Server Actions be secured?
faq.answer: Treat every action as a public endpoint. Authenticate callers, authorize each resource, validate inputs, limit fields, and avoid exposing sensitive results.
